description: Three single-panel cooling-dilatometry (RLC–T) plots that are the last three panels of a five-panel set: the supplied panels correspond to (c) S3, (d) S4 and (e) S5, while (a) S1 and (b) S2 are named in the caption but not present in the supplied images. Every panel plots relative length change RLC (%) on the y-axis against temperature (°C) on the x-axis (100–500 °C) and shows the contraction branch of an austenitization/cooling cycle with a dashed straight-line tangent drawn to the linear contraction segment; the vertical dashed drop marks the tangent–intersection that defines Ms. (c) S3: y-axis 0.0–0.6 %, curve rises from about 0.15 % at 60 °C through a broad hump near 230 °C, tangent intersection at Ms = 258 °C. (d) S4: two superimposed curves, red "S4 (T_A: 1250 °C)" and black "S4 (T_A: 1150 °C)", y-axis 0.0–1.2 %; a small hump near 250–280 °C precedes the inflection, and the dashed tangents give Ms = 310 °C (red) and Ms = 305 °C (black). (e) S5: y-axis 0.0–1.2 %, hump near 250 °C, tangent intersection at Ms = 331 °C, the highest of the three panels. All Ms values are printed as annotation text on the panels.

observations.observation: Each supplied panel is a cooling dilatometry curve with RLC (%) on the y-axis and Temperature (°C) on the x-axis spanning 100 to 500 °C, with a dashed tangent line and a vertical dashed line marking the Ms intersection.
The S3 panel (c) uses a y-axis range of 0.0–0.6 % RLC, whereas the S4 (d) and S5 (e) panels use 0.0–1.2 % RLC.
Panel (c) prints the martensite-start temperature as Ms = 258 °C at the tangent–contraction intersection.
Panel (d) shows two overlaid curves labelled 'S4 (T_A: 1250 °C)' (red) and 'S4 (T_A: 1150 °C)' (black), with printed values Ms = 310 °C and Ms = 305 °C respectively.
Panel (e) prints Ms = 331 °C for sample S5, the highest Ms among the three supplied panels.
In all three panels a small hump/deviation from linear contraction appears before the Ms tangent intersection, in roughly the 220–280 °C range.
The caption states that the tangent–intersection of the linear contraction segment (dashed lines) defines Ms and assigns the panels as (a) S1, (b) S2, (c) S3, (d) S4, (e) S5.
Panels (a) S1 and (b) S2 named in the caption are not present in the supplied image set, so their Ms values cannot be read here.
The citing text states that in S4 Ms decreased only marginally from 310 °C (1250 °C austenitization) to 305 °C (1150 °C austenitization), a 5 °C difference within experimental scatter.
The citing text states that no clear effect of the Ti microalloying addition on Ms was evident.
The citing text states that the relatively high Ms of 331 °C in S5 reflects lower effective carbon in austenite under the chosen condition.
The citing text states that in S1–S3 relatively low Ms values indicate carbon-enriched austenite, with the lowest Ms in S3 linked to extended κ-carbide dissolution.
The citing text states that austempering temperatures were chosen slightly above the measured Ms values to promote bainitic transformation while suppressing martensite.

subfigures.description: Cooling dilatometry curve labelled S3; RLC (%) vs Temperature (°C), y-axis 0.0–0.6 %, x-axis 100–500 °C. The curve rises from ~0.15 % through a broad hump near 230 °C; a dashed tangent to the linear contraction segment intersects the vertical dashed line at the printed value Ms = 258 °C.

Two superimposed cooling dilatometry curves for S4; RLC (%) 0.0–1.2 % vs Temperature (°C) 100–500 °C. Red curve labelled 'S4 (T_A: 1250 °C)' with Ms = 310 °C and black curve labelled 'S4 (T_A: 1150 °C)' with Ms = 305 °C, each with its own dashed tangent line and vertical drop line; a small hump near 250–280 °C precedes the tangent intersection.

Cooling dilatometry curve labelled S5; RLC (%) vs Temperature (°C), y-axis 0.0–1.2 %, x-axis 100–500 °C. Hump near 250 °C; dashed tangent to the linear segment intersects at the printed value Ms = 331 °C, the highest Ms of the three supplied panels.
